metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Ruled out for Sunday's game
metadata.description: Hollins (calf) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: With Hollins unavailable, Romeo Doubs looks like New England's clear No. 1 receiver. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams could all have increased roles in Hollins' absence.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Not seen at Thursday's practice
metadata.description: Hollins (calf) wasn't spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice available to media, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Hollins appears to be missing a second consecutive practice ahead of Sunday's tilt against the Raiders. If Hollins is unable to suit up Sunday, Efton Chism could work alongside Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas in three-receiver, while Hollins' strong blocking may be missed in the running game.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins (calf) not seen practicing Thursday
metadata.description: Mack Hollins was not seen practicing on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: It is a second straight absence for Hollins to begin the week after his early exit last Sunday. He is likely to be sidelined in Week 5, but he'll need to be monitored in practice on Friday to make sure.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins Not Spotted at Thursday's Practice
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) was not spotted at Thursday's practice during the portion open to the media, according to Evan Lazar of the team's official website. Hollins also missed the first practice of the week on Wednesday, so as of now, he is trending in the wrong direction to be available in Week 5 at home against the Las Vegas Raiders. Top wideout A.J. Brown (ankle) remains on Injured Reserve and will miss a fourth straight game this weekend, so the Patriots receiving room could be pretty thinned out against Vegas if Hollins cannot play. The 33-year-old Hollins has merely been a flex play in deeper fantasy leagues, even with Brown out, and he is still searching for his first touchdown of the year. In the three games without Brown, Hollins has caught 11 of his 15 targets for 158 yards. Romeo Doubs will have at least one more week as the top dog at WR for the Pats, and DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III will have bigger roles against the Raiders if Hollins does not play in Week 5.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Not expected to practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that he doesn't anticipate Hollins (calf) practicing Wednesday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Hollins is nursing a calf injury coming out of this past Sunday's win over the Bills, and his availability for the Patriots' Week 5 matchup with the Raiders is in question. If Hollins can't play this weekend, the Patriots will likely turn to Efton Chism to serve as their No. 3 wideout behind Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins (calf) not practicing Wednesday
metadata.description: Mack Hollins will not practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Hollins left last Sunday's game early. His status remains uncertain for Week 5.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins Not Anticipated to Practice Wednesday
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) exited early from the team's Week 4 win over the Bills, leaving the field in obvious discomfort after sustaining a non-contact injury, and head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday that he is not expected to practice with the calf injury. Hollins has been the team's leading receiver through four weeks, and in his absence, Romeo Doubs, fresh off a two-touchdown performance, becomes close to a must-start player as the de facto number one receiver in an offense looking to sustain momentum. Second-year wideout Efton Chism III could also have some flex value in deeper leagues after finishing Sunday's contest with 42 yards and the game-winning touchdown grab, an early candidate for catch of the year.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins without update on calf injury
metadata.description: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel did not have an update on Mack Hollins' calf injury on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Hollins exited Week 4's game against the Bills with a non-contact injury. His status will need to be monitored throughout the week.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Looking iffy for Week 5
metadata.description: Head coach Mike Vrabel said that he expects to know more about Hollins' calf injury later Monday, and the Patriots are uncertain if the wideout will be able to practice "for a couple days," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.
metadata.analysis: Hollins recorded three catches for 53 yards on four targets before exiting in the third quarter of Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills due to the calf issue. The Patriots listed Hollins as questionable to return at the time of his departure, but he never ended up checking back into the contest. More information on the severity of Hollins' injury should be known in the next day or two, but if he ends up being unavailable for next Sunday's game against the Raiders, more reps would be opened up for Efton Chism, who helped fill in for Hollins in the fourth quarter and made an acrobatic 23-yard touchdown grab with just under two minutes remaining to seal the win over Buffalo.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins Could Miss Practice Time With Calf Injury
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) may be sidelined when the team begins practicing for Week 5. Head coach Mike Vrabel told Doug Kyed on Monday that he doesn't know if Hollins will be able to practice for the next couple of days after the veteran left Sunday's win over Buffalo in the third quarter. Hollins caught three of four targets for 53 yards before exiting and now leads New England with 209 receiving yards through four games. Efton Chism III took on a bigger role after Hollins went down and later caught the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. There is still plenty of time before Sunday's matchup with Las Vegas, so Hollins shouldn't be considered doubtful at this point. His practice participation later in the week should give fantasy managers a much better idea of whether the calf injury will cost him any game action.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins hauls in three passes in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Mack Hollins caught 3-of-4 targets for 53 yards in the Patriots win over the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Hollins continues to excel in his role as a chain mover, but the veteran did exit the game with a calf injury. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Exits game with calf injury
metadata.description: Hollins (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Hollins hauled in three passes (on four targets) for 53 yards before exiting for the locker room, where he'll have his calf injury evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry are all in line for more targets from Drake Maye while Hollins is out of the game.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins Questionable to Return With Calf Injury
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills, according to Evan Lazar of Patriots.com. Hollins went down without contact on an incomplete pass during New England's first possession of the second half. He walked off the field before heading to the locker room. Hollins had three catches for 53 yards before leaving after posting six receptions for 87 yards against Jacksonville last week.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins an Intriguing Fantasy Starter Against His Former Team in Week 4
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has emerged as a potentially viable fantasy football starter for Week 4 against the Buffalo Bills. Hollins is the overall WR42 in PPR leagues this year, and he has scored at least nine points in two of his three games so far. The veteran pass-catcher has stepped up as one of Drake Maye's most physical and reliable targets after the Patriots placed AJ Brown (ankle) on injured reserve following the season opener. Brown still has another two-plus weeks on IR, leaving Hollins' fantasy managers with a multi-week opportunity to start him. Hollins' physicality and reliability, which resulted in him earning nine targets last week, should lead to some touchdowns sooner rather than later. He's a strong WR3/flex option this week against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most yards and sixth-most fantasy points to wide receivers this year.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins Makes for an Interesting Deep-League Option
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins stepped up for this offense this past weekend. Hollins hauled in six of his nine targets for 87 yards in the blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Pats are without A.J. Brown (ankle) right now, so they needed someone to step up. Hollins did a nice job on Sunday and figures to earn himself a bigger role in the offense going forward. The 33-year-old clearly has good chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye. Fantasy managers needing wide receiver help in deep leagues should consider adding Hollins ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins leads team in receiving Sunday
metadata.description: Mack Hollins hauled in 6-of-9 targets for 87 yards in Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Hollins was one of the lone bright spots for the Patriots on Sunday. He led the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards against the Jaguars, but that wasn't enough to even keep things close against the Jaguars. He will continue to play a big role for the Patriots moving forward but shouldn't be trusted as a fantasy option at this point in the season.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Six catches during defeat
metadata.description: Hollins caught six of nine targets for 87 yards during Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Hollins saw nearly twice as many targets as the next closest option DeMario Douglas (five), and his 87 yards were his highest total in a regular-season contest since Week 10 of the 2025 campaign. With A.J. Brown (ankle) on injured reserve, someone will have to take the reins as the Patriots' top option at wide receiver, and Hollins certainly showed he's capable of handling a larger workload.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins a Deep-League Streamer with Quarterback's Trust Earned
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins earned the trust of quarterback Drake Maye last season, and that could bode well for his fantasy outlook in Week 3 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Ever since A.J. Brown (ankle) went down in Week 1, Hollins has been operating as the Patriots' de facto No. 2 receiver behind Romeo Doubs. That hasn't really resulted in meaningful fantasy production yet, but he still has a respectable seven targets this season on a 70% snap share. A matchup against the Jaguars could help him break out as a fantasy streamer; Jacksonville has ranked near league average by allowing the 14th-most receiving yards and the 17th-most fantasy points to wide receivers so far in 2026. There are a lot of WR3/flex options to consider in deeper leagues for Week 3, and Hollins is certainly one of them. As of now, he's the WR57 in RotoBaller's latest Week 3 fantasy football rankings.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins has Extended Waiver-Wire Appeal in New England
metadata.description: With New England Patriots top wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) on Injured Reserve and forced to miss at least three more games, Mack Hollins will continue to have a big role in the Patriots' passing attack. The 33-year-old veteran had four catches on five targets for 51 yards in the season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks and disappointed with only two receptions for 18 yards in the Week 2 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in the first game with Brown on the sidelines. Quarterback Drake Maye did not have a good game overall throwing the football against the Steelers, and the positive for Hollins is that he played 71% of the offensive snaps, which was the most among any of New England's receivers. Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas will also be involved more for however long Brown is out, but Hollins should not be ignored as a waiver-wire pickup with short-term upside in the Patriots' offense with Brown sidelined. The former fourth-rounder by the Philadelphia Eagles in 2017 is rostered in only 4% of Yahoo leagues.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Quiet but on field often in Week 2
metadata.description: Hollins caught both of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 20-3 victory over Pittsburgh.
metadata.analysis: After leading the Patriots with 51 receiving yards on four receptions in the team's season opener, Hollins had a more subdued performance versus the Steelers. The veteran wideout was nonetheless on the field often, logging 39 of New England's 55 offensive snaps -- most among the club's wideouts (Romeo Doubs was second with 37 offensive snaps). Although Doubs and DeMario Douglas were listed as the Patriots' starting wideouts, Douglas logged just 26 offensive snaps, so Hollins may have at least temporarily leapfrogged him in the pecking order.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins hauls in two passes in Week 2 win
metadata.description: Patriots WR Mack Hollins caught both of his targets for 18 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Hollins saw his target numbers drop from Week 1, but the passing attack struggled as a whole again. Hollins has a great rapport with QB Drake Maye, which should lead to a potential in increased chances until A.J. Brown returns from injured reserve. Hollins and the Patriots will travel to Jacksonville in Week 3.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins to Benefit From Steady Rapport with Quarterback
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has consistently maintained a role on offense as one of quarterback Drake Maye's most reliable targets, and that shouldn't change anytime soon. Recently, head coach Mike Vrabel said that one of the most important things for a quarterback and wide receiver duo is to "think alike," according to Mike Reiss of ESPN.com. Not only do Hollins and Maye check that box, but they also sit together in meetings, which further reinforces their bond. We've seen this off-field bond translate to a trust factor on the field, as Maye often looks to Hollins when he has nobody open. The two connected for 46 completions, 550 yards, and two touchdowns last year, and Hollins opened 2026 right where he left off with four catches for 51 yards. He should continue to handle a decent volume share going forward with AJ Brown (ankle) on injured reserve. Hollins is a solid speculative waiver wire pickup, but he's only worth considering for the WR3/flex spot in deeper leagues with 14+ teams.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins a Reliable Target with Deep-League Streaming Appeal
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins could get onto the fantasy radar during Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The team recently placed A.J. Brown (ankle) on injured reserve, bumping Hollins up to No. 3 on the depth chart behind Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. Hollins has the most experience of that bunch, and he has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to bail out Drake Maye, earning the young quarterback's trust in high-leverage spots. Doubs may have the big-play upside and Douglas is a high-volume, short-yardage weapon. However, Hollins is more of a playmaker on the perimeter and in contested situations. He had four catches for 51 yards on a 70% snap share in Week 1, and those numbers could also climb even higher in Week 2 now that Brown is sidelined. Hollins ranks as the overall WR56 in RotoBaller's latest fantasy football rankings for Week 2.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins Likely to See Expanded Role
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins stepped up in a big way during the season opener. Hollins was not expected to be a significant part of the offense, but he ended up being one of the lone bright spots. The 33-year-old hauled in four of his five targets for 51 yards in the loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He saw an expanded role in the offense once top wideout A.J. Brown (ankle) exited the contest. It sounds like Brown is going to miss over a month of action, which could lead to a bigger role for Hollins in this offense. Hollins will probably move into a starting role for the Week 2 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. He could be worth stashing in deep leagues while Brown is out.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins leads team in receiving Wednesday
metadata.description: Mack Hollins caught 4-of-5 targets for 51 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: Hollins was one of the lone bright spots for New England on Wednesday night. He stepped up and led the team in receiving in the absence of A.J. Brown (ankle), and he made several important plays which helped to keep them in the game up until the very end. He isn't likely to be fantasy relevant moving forward but should continue to play an important role for the team.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Steps up after Brown injury
metadata.description: Hollins secured four of five targets for 51 yards in the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seahawks on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout was listed as No. 4 on the depth chart heading into the season opener, but Hollins finished as the team leader in receiving yards on the night. Hollins also had a team-high 19-yard reception, and he became much more of a factor after A.J. Brown went down early in the third quarter with an ankle injury. Brown exited the locker room donning a walking boot per Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald, so Hollins could be tasked with an elevated role again in the Week 2 home opener against the Steelers on Sunday, Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins Re-Enters the Deep-League Conversation
metadata.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has a little more room to matter in deeper leagues after Kayshon Boutte was traded to Houston. Hollins already found a way onto the field last season, catching 46 passes for 550 yards and two touchdowns in 15 games before adding 129 yards and another score over New England's final two playoff games. His summer was encouraging, too. Patriots.com noted that Hollins worked with the first-team offense in heavier personnel groupings, where Drake Maye found him repeatedly on play-action throws. The Boutte trade clears out one more receiver, but this is still a crowded room. A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas sit ahead of Hollins on the unofficial depth chart, and Kyle Williams earned a role with a strong preseason. RotoBaller has Hollins at WR91 in half-PPR formats, so this is not a standard-league target. In deeper drafts, though, his blocking, size and situational role give him a slightly cleaner path to usable weeks than he had before the trade.

metadata.title: Mack Hollins - Pair of catches in preseason
metadata.description: Hollins wrapped up the preseason slate with two catches (on four targets) for 24 yards in two outings.
metadata.analysis: When Hollins inked a two-year deal with the Patriots in March 2025, it marked his fifth team in as many seasons. He then managed just seven receptions through the first five games, but from Week 6 through Super Bowl LX, he racked up a 45-637-1 line on 66 targets in 12 appearances, averaging 14.2 yards per catch during that stretch. Even with Stefon Diggs (Commanders) out of the picture this year, Hollins has tougher competition for reps after New England added A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs to a receiving corps that still boasts DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams.
